policies.bottleneck: In 'partial-observation-backtrack' and its mirror, the agent stood on a cell with known, unvisited neighbors (tiles at (1,2)/(2,1) and (2,2)/(1,1)) yet kept speculating out-of-graph left moves, producing 3 'destination is not walkable' blocks, 0 waits, and score 0 in 4 steps; the prior candidate (ex-partial-frontier-neighbor-01) used width/height-bound speculation even when a known frontier transition existed.
policies.rationale: Treat observation.tiles as the known graph and act on it only: if a known neighbor of the agent's cell exists, prefer an unvisited known neighbor (frontier expansion), otherwise backtrack through the least-visited known neighbor (visit counts derived from context.memory action positions plus accepted move destinations). Speculate within width/height bounds only when no known neighbor exists yet, and never retry a direction from a position where context.memory records accepted=false for that exact move. Direction is chosen purely from observed data, so mirrored holdouts behave symmetrically. Returns undefined (defer to baseline) whenever parcels/keys/doors/batteries are visible, energy is zero, or the observation is malformed, protecting the key-door, battery, and delivery holdouts.
policies.expectedMetric: partial-observation-backtrack and partial-observation-backtrack-mirror: achieved=true, score >= 8, 0 'destination is not walkable' blocks (was 3 blocks, score 0 in 4 steps); partial-observation-frontier and frontier-mirror stay achieved at score 8; key-door-delivery (10), battery-return (10), simple-delivery (5), two-parcels (13), detour-delivery (10) unchanged via deferral.

policies.bottleneck: The agent routes toward an uncarried parcel through a door without first collecting the co-located key, so the door blocks 3 consecutive moves in key-door-delivery.
policies.rationale: Evidence shows the key-door-delivery run made 3 blocked 'move right' actions ('A key is required to cross this door') while a key was co-located with the agent at (0,0) and the target parcel at (1,0) sat behind a door at (1,0). Prioritizing collection of the co-located key (an access resource) before routing through the gate satisfies the prerequisite and unblocks delivery. The extension defers (returns undefined) whenever no door is present, no non-co-located pending parcel exists, or no co-located key is available, preserving holdout behavior in simple-delivery, two-parcels, detour-delivery, and battery-return (all have zero doors).
policies.expectedMetric: Blocked transitions in key-door-delivery reduced from 3 to 0 and delivery achieved (score 10 vs 0).

policies.bottleneck: In 'battery-return' the agent committed to a parcel route whose round-trip cost exceeded its energy, so 3 return actions were blocked by exhaustion even though a recharge battery sat directly on the path.
policies.rationale: Add a resource-aware task utility: compute the intended parcel's round-trip cost (2*distance + pickup + putdown). When that cost exceeds current energy and a battery is co-located, the recharge pickup is a net-positive moment, so select it now instead of committing to the parcel route; this refuels before spending energy on delivery. Defers (undefined) whenever energy is untracked, a parcel is already carried, no parcel is open, the route is already affordable, or no battery is co-located, protecting holdout behavior.
policies.expectedMetric: battery-return: achieved true, score 10 (was 0), energy-blocked actions 0 (was 3); no regressions on key-door-delivery, simple-delivery, two-parcels, detour-delivery.
policies.source: (context) => { const o = context.observation; if (!o || !o.me) return undefined; if (typeof o.energy !== 'number') return undefined; const parcels = o.parcels || []; if (parcels.some((p) => p.carriedBy)) return undefined; const open = parcels.filter((p) => !p.carriedBy); if (open.length === 0) return undefined; const dist = (a, b) => Math.abs(a.x - b.x) + Math.abs(a.y - b.y); const best = open.reduce((a, b) => ((b.reward || 0) > (a.reward || 0) ? b : a)); const d = dist(o.me, best); const roundTrip = 2 * d + 2; if (o.energy >= roundTrip) return undefined; const batteries = o.batteries || []; if (!batteries.some((b) => dist(o.me, b) === 0)) return undefined; return { action: { kind: 'pickup' }, confidence: 0.85, rationale: 'Best parcel round-trip cost ' + roundTrip + ' exceeds energy ' + o.energy + '; a co-located battery is a net-positive recharge, so pick it up before committing to the parcel route.' }; }

policies.bottleneck: On partial-observation runs with no visible task objects, the agent emits consecutive waits and scores 0 (both frontier and mirror cases) because nothing drives discovery of new tiles.
policies.rationale: In 'partial-observation-frontier' and 'partial-observation-frontier-mirror', observation shows only the agent's own tile, zero parcels/keys/doors/batteries, and the baseline waited twice ('No visible parcel can be selected'). The fix activates only when no task object is visible, then picks the first unvisited in-bounds neighbor computed from optional width/height bounds plus positions recorded in context.memory (array of {x,y,action,module}), so the direction is derived per-instance rather than constant and mirrors safely. It returns undefined whenever a parcel, key, door, or battery is visible (protecting key-door-delivery, battery-return, simple-delivery, two-parcels, detour-delivery) and waits only when the local frontier is exhausted or energy is exactly 0.
policies.expectedMetric: partial-observation-frontier and partial-observation-frontier-mirror: waits drop from 2 to at most 1, first action becomes a valid in-bounds move, score goes from 0 to > 0; all five achieved benchmarks remain achieved.
policies.source: (context) => { const o = context && context.observation; if (!o || !o.me) return undefined; const me = o.me; if ((o.parcels && o.parcels.length) || (o.keys && o.keys.length) || (o.doors && o.doors.length) || (o.batteries && o.batteries.length)) return undefined; const visited = new Set(); visited.add(me.x + ',' + me.y); const mem = context && Array.isArray(context.memory) ? context.memory : []; for (const m of mem) { if (m && m.x !== undefined && m.y !== undefined) visited.add(m.x + ',' + m.y); } const inB = (x, y) => (o.width === undefined || (x >= 0 && x < o.width)) && (o.height === undefined || (y >= 0 && y < o.height)); const dirs = [['down', 0, 1], ['left', -1, 0], ['right', 1, 0], ['up', 0, -1]]; const cand = dirs.filter((d) => inB(me.x + d[1], me.y + d[2]) && !visited.has((me.x + d[1]) + ',' + (me.y + d[2]))); if (!cand.length) return { action: { kind: 'wait', reason: 'frontier-exhausted' }, confidence: 0.5, rationale: 'All in-bounds neighbors are already visited; no unvisited frontier remains.' }; if (o.energy === 0) return { action: { kind: 'wait', reason: 'no-energy-for-move' }, confidence: 0.6, rationale: 'Energy is zero and every move costs energy, so defer the exploration move.' }; const c = cand[0]; return { action: { kind: 'move', direction: c[0] }, confidence: 0.7, rationale: 'No visible task; expanding the partial-observation frontier to the first unvisited in-bounds neighbor (' + c[0] + ') using width/height bounds and memory.' }; }
